mappings.note: Both statements swap the materials and influences of the Mathura and Gandhara schools. Art history under the goal; LO-103 covers buildings, not sculpture.
Statements on the Muvendar, the antiquity of Sangam literature and Chera maritime trade. Mixed period recall, so the goal.
Names Vasudeva as the deity of the Heliodorus dedication. A fact read off an inscription; LO-104 would need the emergence of the devotional movement to be analysed rather than the name supplied.
Shaka Samvat as a calendar era begun under Shaka rule. Chronology, which no LO covers.
The compilation of the epics read as evidence of a lively literary culture. A cultural-development judgement under the goal.
Pushyamitra Shunga as assassin and founder. Dynastic recall; the companion item on his ashvamedha carries LO-101 because that one is about asserting power.
Dates the Mauryan break-up to about 185 BCE. Chronology under the goal.
Names the 'Age of Reorganisation'. A period label, not an administrative measure.
Names the matrimonial alliance as a marriage-based pact between royal houses - an instrument of statecraft. Same reading as its MCQ twin.
Names the ashvamedha as the rite Pushyamitra used to assert power. A political claim to sovereignty, so LO-101 rather than the religion outcome.
The Yoga Sutras as Patanjali's Shunga-period text. Intellectual history and a source of the age.

Names the Bharhut Stupa for the railings and reliefs the Shungas added - a development in religious architecture and its ornament. Kept with the other Bharhut item under LO-103, the frame's only monument outcome.
The Satavahanas, also called Andhras, as the Deccan power after the Mauryas. Dynastic and regional recall.
Names a Satavahana capital. Historical geography; no governance is described.
Coins as the objects depicting ships. A point about numismatic evidence, the goal's sources clause.
Names Gautamiputra Satakarni, the king with his mother's name. Dynastic and social recall.
Names the Naneghat caves as the find-spot of a queen's inscriptions. A source-location item; the companion item on toll collection there carries LO-101 because it concerns revenue.
The Chedis rising in Kalinga after the Mauryas. Dynastic succession under the goal.
Kharavela as the Chedi king of the Hathigumpha record. A person-and-source recall.
Locates the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves near Bhubaneswar. Historical geography; the item asks where, not how they were cut, so not LO-103.
Names Sangam literature as the oldest Tamil corpus. The sources clause of the goal.
'Sangam' as an assembly of poets. Literary vocabulary under the goal.
Names the three crowned kingdoms of the Sangam age. Dynastic recall, not administration.
Karikala as the builder of the Kallanai. A recall of who; the item on what the dam achieved carries LO-101 instead.
'Keralaputra' as the Cheras' other name. Dynastic naming under the goal.
The Indo-Greeks as the group that followed Alexander's satraps. Political chronology.
The Shakas as the Indo-Scythian invaders after the Indo-Greeks. Sequence of dynasties under the goal.
Shaka Samvat as the era adopted for the national calendar. Chronology, the same lane as the offset item.
The Kushanas as the Central Asian dynasty ruling north India. Dynastic and geographical recall.
Kanishka, known from the headless statue. A ruler identified through an artefact, so the goal's sources clause.
Explains the period label through fragmentation into competing kingdoms and invasions. Period characterisation, the short-answer twin of the MCQ.

The ashvamedha's procedure - a horse roaming, unchallenged territory absorbed, resistance meaning battle - is a mechanism of territorial claim backed by force. The fullest LO-101 reading of the rite in this chapter.
The carved railings and Jataka reliefs at Bharhut cited as evidence of Shunga patronage of religious architecture. Not CG-SST2, because the answer rests on what was built and carved.
Wide coin distribution and ship imagery as evidence of trade - inference from numismatic sources. Not LO-101, since no state measure is involved.
The matronymic naming system and what it suggests about queens' standing. Social history read from inscriptions.

The Hathigumpha record of Kharavela's military victories and public works is a ruler's account of his own measures of rule. Not CG-SST2: the inscription is the vehicle, but the question asks what his rule consisted of.
What Sangam literature is and why it matters to historians - the clearest 'types of sources' item in the chapter.
Narrates the Kannagi story from the Silappadikaram. Literary and cultural history under the goal.

The Kallanai's significance - diverting the Kaveri to irrigate the delta and support rice cultivation - is a ruler's public work and its effect on the realm. Distinguished from the two recall items that only ask who built it.
Chera exports of pepper, timber, ivory and pearls and trade with Rome and West Asia. Trade history; no LO covers commerce.
